standing: OPEN — the two code defects are FIXED; two design questions are Akien's and are why this stays open
why: The emit-chokepoint is the physics that makes a workflow cursor real (Law 4). Measured 2026-07-26, only 6 of 17 staged nodes could pass through it — and one of the six that 'passed' was handed a FABRICATED path. So the cursor, the field every reader turns into 'where is this boat', was policy on 11 of 17 nodes and fiction on a 12th.

occurrences.identity: cairn/base/transitions.py::parse_workflow — the RULES rung of the emit-chokepoint
occurrences.location: cairn/base/transitions.py:100-107 (the path walk); surfaced while binding cairn/base/needs.py to a node's stage vocabulary (tickets/stage-needs.json child a)
occurrences.code: for seg in rest.split('->'): sm = _STATE_RE.match(seg); if not sm: break; path.append(sm.group(1))
occurrences.expected: The path is the states before the trailing note. state-machine-physics.json is a code-seam@v1 node, so its path is the 6-state canonical vocabulary: THINKME TICKETME BUILDME PROVEME LEARNME PROVED.
occurrences.actual: 9 states: THINKME TICKETME BUILDME PROVEME LEARNME PROVED **BUILDME REVIEWME PROVED**. The walk split on '->' across the ENTIRE remainder and stopped only at a segment not starting with a capitalised token — so the ticket's own note, which mentions the concept-piece workflow 'THINKME -> REVIEWME -> PROVED' as a child, fed its states onto this node's path. No exception, no warning.
occurrences.fatality: SILENT WRONG ANSWER — the costly direction (Law 7). Every reader of `path` was handed fiction: `here`, `legal_targets` (which derives the legal set BY INDEX into the path), and therefore `validate_transition`. A phantom trailing PROVED means the last real state is no longer treated as the end of the voyage.
occurrences.trace: parse_workflow(state) -> path=[...9 states...] -> Workflow(cursor=2) -> legal_targets() indexes a path that does not exist -> _conform() compares against the registered 6-state path -> MalformedWorkflow('string path does not conform'). The refusal names the SYMPTOM (a drifted string) and blames the ticket, when the parser built the drift itself.

occurrences.identity: the six nodes cast 2026-07-26 via /sorted — challenge-fires-at-intent, clearance-leaves-a-trace, demo-gate, inference-host-wiring, plan-inspector, quarry-index
occurrences.code: "state": "code-seam@v1: THINKME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> PROVED   (CAST 2026-07-26 via /sorted; cursor at BUILDME. Leaf. ...)"
occurrences.expected: A cursor a machine can read — the bracketed state the parser requires, on the class's declared vocabulary.
occurrences.actual: NO BRACKETS ANYWHERE. The cursor existed only as the English sentence 'cursor at BUILDME' inside the note, and the path had TICKETME DELETED to signal the leaf fork. Both halves are unreadable: parse_workflow raised MalformedWorkflow('no bracketed cursor'), and had it not, _conform would have refused the shortened path as drift.
occurrences.fatality: LOUD when finally read (a raise), but nothing was reading it — the strings sat on disk for a day looking correct to every human reader. Discovered only because a new consumer (needs.py) tried to bind needs to the stage vocabulary.
occurrences.trace: /sorted renders the workflow string as prose -> the ticket looks well-formed to a reader -> no proof parses staged tickets except one tooth that SEARCHES for a conformant ticket and skips non-matching ones -> the malformity is invisible until a consumer arrives.

the_defect: Two independent faults with one shape: the workflow cursor was never actually machine-readable, so nothing enforced it. (1) THE PARSER over-consumed its own trailing prose, fabricating states from any arrow inside a note. (2) /sorted WRITES A CURSOR NO MACHINE CAN READ — a prose sentence instead of brackets — and expresses the leaf fork by DELETING the skippable summons from the path, when the skip is properly a cursor POSITION (legal_targets already derives the fork from skippable_summons; the vocabulary is the class's and does not shrink per instance).
why_it_is_a_trouble_and_not_just_a_bug: The chokepoint is the flagship Law 4 claim — 'the state vocabulary is physics, not /sorted's prose', in that proof's own words. It was prose on 11 of 17 nodes. And the PROOF DID NOT CATCH IT, which is the part that generalises: test_transitions.py's live-ticket tooth scans for a ticket whose path already equals canonical and skips the rest, so every malformed node was silently excluded from the sample and the tooth passed BECAUSE of the defect. A proof that skips the malformed case is a hollow pass (Law 8) — the same shape as the append-door trouble, where the door enforced everything except the thing that mattered.
resolution_so_far: BOTH CODE DEFECTS FIXED AND PROVEN, 2026-07-26. (1) parse_workflow now stops at the first state carrying prose, so a note cannot extend the path. Regression tooth: test_prose_after_the_last_state_cannot_feed_phantom_states_onto_the_path, which asserts the path EXACTLY on a string built to carry the trap — and was verified non-hollow by reverting the fix and watching it fail (Law 8, checked rather than assumed). (2) The six strings were re-rendered onto the canonical 6-state vocabulary with the cursor in brackets at the position their own prose claimed; no cursor was MOVED, so this is a repair of a malformed rendering, not a transition (no clearance needed). Fleet conformance went 6/17 -> 13/17, measured by re-running the scan. RE-MEASURED 2026-07-31, after the intentions rename: ALL 65 live tickets now parse through parse_workflow — up from the 13-of-17 above. The last five were repaired this day, using render() as the trouble's own the_fix_when_taken prescribes: two were SELF-CONTRADICTING (chart.json bracketed [PROVED] while its own note said 'cursor at TICKETME'; host-seam-installer.json bracketed [THINKME] against a note saying TICKETME — the bracket was template residue in both, and both were being READ WRONG by every census, which is the silent-wrong-answer direction Law 7 cares about) and three were PRE-SCHEMA v0 word-states ('validated'/'building') that no bracket walk could see at all; those three carry `migrated_from` with the old word verbatim, so the drop is not silent. THE STANDING IOU IS UNCHANGED: /sorted still hand-writes the string, so the next cast can reintroduce this. What is now also measured is that hand-repair does not scale — five in one sitting, found only because a census was run for another reason.
the_fix_when_taken: The remaining half is /sorted itself: it must RENDER the string through cairn/base/transitions.py (render() already exists and emits exactly the canonical bracketed form) instead of hand-writing prose. Until it does, the next cast reintroduces this trouble — which is the definition of an unclosed gate (Law 4). Filed as the natural first tooth of tickets/challenge-fires-at-intent.json's sibling work on the cast path; not built here because /sorted is a skill node with its own charter and gates.
open_and_akiens: concept-piece HAS NO MACHINE-READABLE WORKFLOW AT ALL. node_classes/concept-piece.json carries no `workflow_versions`, so ticket-and-task.json's 'concept-piece@v1' string can never validate ('unknown workflow version v1, known: []'). Worse, that string claims THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> PROVED while state-machine-physics.json says the concept-piece workflow is THINKME -> REVIEWME -> PROVED. Those contradict, and the class-store charter says a class definition is RATIFIED BY AKIEN (signature gate) — so CC does not get to pick. Blocks 1 of 17.

THREE PRE-ERA NODES carry a bare prose state instead of a workflow string: cc-learning-store ('building'), learning-as-a-pattern ('building'), default-superclaude-to-200k ('validated'). They predate the state-machine and were never migrated. Migrating them means choosing a class and a cursor for each — an authoring act on someone else's record, so it is asked, not assumed. Blocks 3 of 17.

Law 7 — the parser's fault was a SILENT wrong answer, the direction that costs most
Law 3 — 'only 6 of 17 could pass' is measured by a scan, not estimated; the same scan re-run is what shows 13
Law 8 — the guarding proof passed by SKIPPING the malformed cases; the new tooth was checked against the reverted fix so it cannot pass hollow
I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass — both occurrences carry identity/location/code/expected/actual/fatality/trace so no re-run is needed to act
kin: CairnCommons/troubles/append-door-has-no-schema-gate.json — the same shape one layer over: a single door that enforced everything except the thing that mattered, and a malformity that surfaced only downstream
CairnCommons/tickets/state-machine-physics.json — owns the chokepoint; its own string was the one parsing to 9 states
CairnCommons/tickets/stage-needs.json — child a is the consumer whose arrival exposed all of this
cairn/base/needs.py — binds needs to the stage vocabulary, which is why it could not be built on a cursor that was prose
found_how: Not by inspection and not by a red: by BUILDING A CONSUMER. needs.py validates that a declared need attaches to a stage the node actually has, which meant parsing 17 live workflow strings for the first time. The scan that answered 'can this bind?' answered 'the cursor is not readable' instead. The generalisation worth keeping: a claim that something is physics is only tested when a second reader depends on it — the first reader can be wrong in the same direction as the writer.
